description: We are Sahel Stardust00001, a team of software engineers spread across Abuja (Nigeria), Togo and Senegal. Over the 48 hours of the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we collaborate remotely to turn NASA open data into practical solutions. What unites us is a love of code and the drive to take on the next frontier from West Africa.
summary:
unior Astronaut: Mars Survival is a browser-based game that teaches children aged 7–12 the real trade-offs behind running a Mars outpost. Players lead a four-astronaut base for 12 sols (Martian days). Each sol they share a limited energy budget between life support, a greenhouse, a radiation shield and communications. No choice is free: powering the greenhouse leaves less energy for the shield, and cutting communications means no early warning from Earth about dangers such as dust storms, leaks or solar flares.

Solar flare events are based on archived NASA DONKI space-weather data, so the radiation risk players face reflects real solar activity. At the end of each mission, a debrief shows the key decisions that led to success or failure and adds a short science fact, so failure becomes a lesson, not a punishment.

The game needs no download or account, works on phones, and is available in French and English. It makes the hard choices of space exploration concrete and playable for young learners.
details:
What it does. Mission Outpost is a browser game for kids aged 7–12 who command a small Mars outpost (Jezero Crater) for seven days. Each day, players split 100 energy units between four stations: Life (air, food, crew health), Shield (reduces simulated radiation exposure), Communications (Earth alerts and advice) and Science (research points). Real archived NASA space-weather events drive the story: solar storms arrive, and players must decide whether to spend energy on protection or on keeping the outpost running. A daily report explains what happened and why, and exact numbers are available under "See the details." Benefits and expected impact. No choice is free: more shielding means less energy for life support or science. Players experience the trade-offs mission planners face and see how real solar activity connects to decisions. The educational impact is an intended goal, not yet a measured result. Tools. React, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind CSS; animated SVG and CSS visuals; Vitest for the game engine; a Python script to fetch NASA DONKI data; the optional Web Speech API for read-aloud. No special hardware. Built with VS Code, GitHub and GitHub Copilot. Creativity. A living Mars base replaces dashboards of numbers: four expressive astronauts show crew health, a tank and greenhouse show resources, a bubble shows the shield, and a Geiger-style meter shows radiation. A mascot gives short hints. What we considered. Young players, so only three core resources and plain-language explanations with a glossary. Accessibility: mobile-first, bilingual, keyboard-friendly, reduced-motion friendly, never color-only. Low barrier: no download, account or live API required. Honesty: archived data is labeled as archive; energy costs and outcomes are game parameters, not NASA measurements or forecasts; ISS data is not presented as a Mars reading.
https://outpostmission.netlify.app
